sections.title: Stephen's Speech to the Sanhedrin
observations: Stephen begins his defense by recounting the history of Israel, starting with Abraham, to show that God's plan has always been to work through His chosen people, even when they were in foreign lands.
He emphasizes God's covenant with Abraham and the promise of land, highlighting the faith of Abraham who obeyed God without knowing where he was going.
Stephen's recounting of Joseph's story illustrates how God's chosen ones often face rejection, paralleling his own situation.

sections.title: The Rejection of Moses
observations: Stephen points to Moses as a deliverer who was rejected by his own people, drawing a parallel to the rejection of Jesus.
He highlights Moses' early life and his attempt to help the Israelites, which was met with hostility, foreshadowing the rejection of Christ.

sections.title: The Vision of Heaven
observations: As Stephen is being stoned, he sees a vision of Jesus standing at the right hand of God, which serves as a powerful affirmation of his faith and the truth of his message.
His final words echo the words of Jesus on the cross, demonstrating his commitment to forgiveness even in the face of death.

importantVerses.commentary: Stephen, filled with the Holy Spirit, gazes into heaven and sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God, affirming the divine approval of his testimony.
Stephen's prayer for forgiveness for his attackers reflects the heart of Christ and the essence of Christian forgiveness, even in the face of persecution.

questions: What does Stephen's speech reveal about the continuity of God's plan throughout history?
How does the rejection of Moses serve as a foreshadowing of the rejection of Jesus?
What significance does Stephen's vision of Jesus have for understanding the nature of Christ's authority?
In what ways can we apply Stephen's example of forgiveness in our own lives?
